findings.title: Storage and legacy duration metrics are recorded to the wrong collectors
findings.body:
Several methods in `DualWriterMode3` call the wrong metric recorder:
- In `Create` (line 45), when `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- In `Update` (line 129), when `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- In `DeleteCollection` (line 166), after `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` finishes in the background goroutine, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

This skews latency and error metrics between unified storage and legacy storage.

findings.title: Delete passes object name instead of options.Kind to recordStorageDuration
findings.body: On line 106 in `Delete`, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the resource `name` as the `kind` argument instead of `options.Kind`. This records each individual object name in the `kind` metric label, producing incorrect labels and unbounded metric cardinality.

findings.title: Async legacy writes derive context from the request context and get canceled when the request returns
findings.body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutine creates its timeout context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)` directly from the request `ctx`, and the outer function immediately returns. When the HTTP handler finishes serving the request, the server cancels the request `ctx`, which immediately cancels the derived context in the background goroutine and aborts in-flight legacy storage writes. The goroutines should detach from parent cancellation (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`) before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Delete stores d.Log instead of the enriched logger in context
findings.body: In `Delete`, line 96 creates `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 calls `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. Any downstream code extracting the logger from `ctx` loses the `name`, `kind`, and `method` log fields.

findings.title: Mode 3 unit tests share a single mock between Legacy and Storage and do not await async legacy writes
findings.body: In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, `ls := legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `us := storageMock{m, s}` wrap the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` instance, and the write tests (`Create`, `Delete`, `DeleteCollection`, `Update`) return without waiting for or asserting on the background goroutine that writes to `Legacy`. As a result, `TestMode3_Create`'s error case (line 40) configures `setupLegacyFn` to test a unified storage failure and only passes because both mocks share `m`, while `TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection` do not verify whether `Legacy` is called at all.
